question.problem:
The rate at which water flows into a tank is given by the function

$$
r(t)=6t+10,
$$

where $r(t)$ is measured in liters per hour and $t>0$ is the time in hours since $1\,\text{p.m}.$
Water is also draining from the tank at a steady rate of $8$ liters per hour.

If there were $200$ liters of water in the tank at $1\,\text{p.m},$ how many liters of water will be there at $5\,\text{p.m}?$

There will be 
{{field-1}}  liters of water in the tank at $5\,\text{p.m}.$
question.worked_solution:
Water is flowing into the tank at a rate of $6t+10$ liters per hour and is draining at a rate of $8$ liters per hour. Therefore, the **rate of change** in the amount of water (call it $R(t)$) is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(t) & =r(t)-8 \\  & =6t+10-8 \\  & =6t+2.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the **total amount of water** after $t$ hours (call it $T(t)$), we apply the second fundamental theorem of calculus:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =T(0)+{\int }_{0}^{t}R(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =200+{\int }_{0}^{t}(6x+2)\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

To ensure that $T$ is a function of $t$ only, we use a different variable ($x$) for the integration. 

To find out the amount of water after $4$ hours ($5\,\text{p.m}$), we substitute $t=4$ into the above and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(4) & =200+{\int }_{0}^{4}(6x+2)\,\text{d}x \\  & =200+(3{x}^{2}+2x){|}_{0}^{4} \\  & =200+[(3\cdot 16+8)-0] \\  & =200+56 \\  & =256\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, there will be $256$ liters of water in the tank at $5\,\text{p.m}.$
